svg.text: The block's 128 × 128 square of y, and the 256 threads that make it
Each cell is 8 rows × 4 columns; the number is the thread that makes it. Every thread makes two cells: two halves, 64 columns apart.
column 64: the second halves start here
Thread n makes rows 8 × (n ÷ 16) … +7 and columns 4 × (n mod 16) … +3, and the same 4 columns + 64.
thread 0 (purple): rows 0–7, columns 0–3 and 64–67. thread 17 (green): rows 8–15, columns 4–7 and 68–71.
Its 8 × 8 = 64 values are its sums[8][8], kept in registers from the first step to the last.
Light purple: one warp, threads 0–31, the 32 threads that run each instruction together: rows 0–15.
Why two halves (run 4): at each i, threads 0–15 read their columns of the W piece. As two halves, those are
64 neighbouring floats, every shared memory bank used equally (Figure 7).
